history.new: For every N, the instances y <= N - 2 of x*(y+1) = (x*y)*(x+1) force at most one anchored table (Laver's recursion; written proof in proofs/paper/C17.md). At N = 2^n it is the Laver table A_n, which satisfies the full instance including the wrap-around y = N - 1. For every N <= 4096 (EXP-C17-03, and independently the Skeptic's C program) the full instance has a model exactly at the powers of 2, so for these N left-distributivity of an anchored table is decided by an O(N^2) check.
history.old: For 2 <= N <= 10, an anchored magma satisfies x*(y+1) = (x*y)*(x+1) for all x, y mod N exactly when N is 2, 4 or 8 and the magma is the Laver table; so for these N, left-distributivity of an anchored table is decided by an O(N^2) check.
